newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended slightly higher in quiet trade. Our prediction that world sugar production in 1996/97 may rise to 126.6 million tonnes, up from 123.1 million tonnes the previous year, had no discernible impact on prices. At the close prices ranged from $0.70 to $0.10 a tonne up. December closed $0.40 higher at $325.50. In New York raw sugar futures settled a thinly-traded session weaker. March lost five points to close at 10.88 cents/lb, while May shed four points to close at 10.80 cents/lb. The back months lost between 1 and 3 points.

BRAZIL - Our estimate of Brazilian sugar production in 1996/97 (June/May) of 15.022 million tonnes, raw value, up from 13.636 million tonnes produced in 1995/96 drew heavy criticism from sources within Brazil. Jose Pilon, president of the Sao Paulo Sugar and Alcohol Industry Association (AIAA), said that the figure for 1996/97 is too high and exaggerated and that the Association's most optimistic figure is for a little over 13 million tonnes. The AIAA also said that it does not agree with the Licht figure for the 1995/96 crop which it puts at around 12.4 million tonnes. Analyst Aloisio Sotero of independent consultants DataNet-Agri Commodities said that the Licht figure is an over-estimate which reflects the view of producers. However, what the critics apparently have overlooked is that our figures are in raw value and not tel quel. Just for the record our figures in tel quel for 1996/97 and 1995/96 are 13.900 and 12.625 million tonnes, respectively. Of course it is extremely difficult to assess the Brazilian crop at this stage, but if our critics are talking tel quel, then the differences are not that great.

SOUTH AFRICA - South African sugar production in 1996/97 (May/April) may be lower than had been expected. According to industry sources the total this season could reach 2.37 million tonnes, tel quel, down from an earlier estimate of 2.44 million tonnes and last year's figure of 1.67 million tonnes. In spite of the reduction in crop expectations the 1996/97 season could be the best in 12 years, industry sources said.

UNITED STATES - Sugar imports in July 1996 jumped to 369,044 tonnes, raw value, sharply up on last year's 209,173 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first 10 months of 1995/96 (October/July) up to 1.83 million tonnes against 1.15 million tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1994/95 reached 1.56 million tonnes against 1.81 million tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of origin in October/July 1995/96 were Guatemala with 259,322 tonnes raws against 67,315 tonnes, Brazil with 253,009 tonnes compared to 171,747, the Dominican Republic with 217,871 tonnes compared to 206,591 tonnes and Costa Rica with 163,236 tonnes against 24,597 tonnes. Canada continued to be the largest white sugar supplier shipping 35,994 tonnes against 57,752 tonnes. Sugar exports in July 1996 amounted to 28,202 tonnes, down from 56,950 tonnes exported in July 1995. This brought cumulative exports in October/July 1995/96 up to 267,036 tonnes, down from 432,356 tonnes shipped in the corresponding period the previous year. Total exports in 1994/95 amounted to 504,854 tonnes against 485,708 tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of destination in October/July 1995/96 were Jamaica with 32,406 tonnes whites against 25,487 tonnes, Haiti with 31,766 tonnes against 53,200 tonnes, Canada with 31,650 tonnes against 113,868 tonnes and Turkey with 26,186 tonnes compared to 28,800 tonnes.

MALAYSIA - Sugar imports in June 1996 amounted to 87,300 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 102,369 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first half of 1996 (January/June) up to 503,467 tonnes against 458,661 tonnes in January/June 1995. Total imports in 1995 reached the record high of 1.03 million tonnes against 959,518 tonnes in 1994. Major countries of origin in January/June 1996 were Thailand with 357,100 tonnes raws against 236,165 tonnes and Australia with 121,367 tonnes, down from 182,230 tonnes. Sugar exports in June 1996 amounted to 9,940 tonnes against 7,546 tonnes in June 1995. This brought cumulative exports in January/June 1996 up to 55,184 tonnes against 48,662 in January/June 1995. Total exports in 1995 amounted to 123,561 tonnes against 159,525 in 1994. Major countries of destination in January/June 1996 were Singapore with 32,256 tonnes whites and Indonesia with 13,862 tonnes.
